summary.text: King of Sparta, husband of Helen and brother of Agamemnon, whose broken marriage summoned the Achaeans to Troy and whose return wandered through Egypt.
summary.citation: Odyssey 4.1–14; Epitome 2.16, 3.3–12, 6.29; Fabulae 118; Description of Greece 2.18.6

story.text: Apollodorus calls Menelaus a son of Atreus and Aerope. He married Helen, received the Spartan kingship from Tyndareus, and called on Agamemnon when Paris carried Helen away.
Homer finds him home in Sparta celebrating two marriages: Hermione, Helen's only child, was being sent to Neoptolemus, while Megapenthes, Menelaus' son by a slave woman, received his own bride.

Storms drove Menelaus through Crete, Libya, Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Egypt. Apollodorus reports a tradition in which he recovered the real Helen from Proteus after Troy had contained only a cloud phantom; Hyginus instead has Proteus teach him how to appease the gods and return in the eighth year.

Pausanias records that Sparta preferred Orestes' Tyndarid claim over Nicostratus and Megapenthes, sons of Menelaus by a slave woman. The succession therefore passed through Hermione rather than Menelaus' sons.
